earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog med: only wordlist-or-less items (Moszkowski 1911-13, Galis 1955, Smits & Voorhoeve 1998); no grammar or phonology exists.

sources.citation: Kluge, Angela. 2017. A grammar of Papuan Malay. (Studies in Diversity Linguistics 11). Berlin: Language Science Press. sec. 1.4 p.13 and Appendix C.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Not about Bagusa phonology; states the documentation situation: 'For the remaining eight languages no resources are available except for their listing in the Ethnologue (Lewis, Simons & Fennig 2016a) and Glottolog (Nordhoff et al. 2013): Bagusa, Betaf, Jofotek-Bromnya, Keijar, Kwerba Mamberamo, Kwinsu, Trimuris, and Wares.' Appendix C table: no survey, lexicon, grammar or literacy items for Bagusa [bqb].

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page bagu1251 (refs: Donohue 2005; Moszkowski 1911-12, 1913; Jongejans 1922; Smits & Voorhoeve 1998; Galis 1955; Du Buy 1955; DeVries 1985 'Nupuk (Bagusa)' 5 pp wordlist; subclassification comment citing DeVries & DeVries 1991:58, Oosterwal 1967)
sources.note: Glottolog's most extensive description = wordlist or less; no grammar, sketch or phonology listed.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Pacific Linguistics B-31. Canberra: ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-B31 (ANU hdl 1885/146481)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bagusa has no entry of its own; it appears only as one of Van der Leeden's tribal names under no. 68 KWERBA (printed p.37). Wordlist appendix key, printed p.92: 'Stress and pitch are not indicated.'

sources.citation: OLAC: Resources in and about the Bagusa language [bqb] (language-archives.org, up-to-date as of 2025-11-03; Internet Archive copy 2026-02-10)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only three items: Glottolog 5.2, Ethnologue 2018, LINGUIST List. No SIL archive item, no description of any kind.

sources.citation: Clouse, Duane, Mark Donohue & Felix Ma. 2002. Survey report of the north coast of Irian Jaya. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2002-078. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonology given only for Airoran/Samarokena. Bagusa appears only on the map, in the Kwerba-subfamily tree ('Bagusa Kwerba-Aurimi Trimuris Kauwera Kwerba-Mam.') and as current occupant of Kapeso/Suaseso on Lake Rombebai (sec. 4.2). No Bagusa data, nothing on its stress. References cite DeVries 1991 'Kwerba' ms and Kim 1999 'Kwerba phonology' ms (SIL Abepura).

sources.citation: De Vries, James A. & Sandra A. De Vries. 1997. An overview of Kwerba verb morphology. In A. Pawley (ed.), Papers in Papuan linguistics No. 3, 1-35. Pacific Linguistics A-87. Canberra: ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-A87.1 (ANU hdl 1885/253642)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: online with a university library login
sources.note: Describes Kwerba of Aurimi (kwer1263), not Bagusa; p.1 lists Bagusa only as a 'closely related language' (with Nopuk, Kauwerawec, Airoran). No phonology section; only an incidental remark that the transitional syllable ra is 'weakly stressed' (p.5). Nothing on Bagusa stress.

sources.citation: [Moszkowski, Max] Anonymous. 1913. Woerterverzeichnisse von Papua-Sprachen aus Hollaendisch-Neuguinea. Anthropos 8: 254-259 (archive.org item anthropos_1913_8, scanned text).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Four-column wordlist (Borumessu / Koassa / Pauwi / Suedfluss) from the Mamberamo; forms carry acute accent marks on vowels but there is no prose on accent/Betonung. Glottolog files it under Bagusa; identity of any column with modern Bagusa is not stated in the source.

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark. n.d. Warembori grammar sketch (MPG-held manuscript, text held by the project)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ethnographic mentions only ('Bagusa is a variety of western Kwerba'; Warembori exonym Putampa); no Bagusa language data.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of Northwest New Guinea. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area, 433-568. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: publisher record (DOI); no open copy and no library e-access found (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Most recent survey of the Tor-Kwerba area; would confirm (second-hand) whether anything is known of Kwerba-family prosody.

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark. 2005. Syntactic and lexical factors conditioning the diffusion of sound change. Oceanic Linguistics 44(2): 427-442.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: online with a university library login (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Only modern linguist-collected Bagusa (and other Kwerba-family) data in print, from Donohue's 1998 Mamberamo fieldwork; a transcription note or footnote on stress in Bagusa/Kwerba is the single realistic place a first-hand remark could exist.

sources.citation: Kim, Yon-Soo. 1999. Kwerba phonology. Unpublished ms. Abepura: SIL; and DeVries, Jim. 1991. Kwerba. UNCEN-SIL ms. Abepura.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Phonology of Kwerba-Aurimi, the closest described relative (Bagusa is 'a variety of western Kwerba' per Donohue); would give the family's stress pattern, though not Bagusa itself.

sources.citation: Smits, Leo & C. L. Voorhoeve. 1998. The J. C. Anceaux collection of wordlists of Irian Jaya languages, B: Non-Austronesian (Papuan) languages (Part II). Irian Jaya Source Materials. Leiden/Jakarta: DSALCUL/IRIS. 250 pp.

sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Contains the Anceaux-era Bagusa wordlists; transcriptions may carry stress marks and the editors' introduction may comment on them.

sources.citation: DeVries, Jim. 1985. Nupuk (Bagusa). 5 pp. SIL Irian Jaya survey wordlist (Glottolog ref 570520).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only Bagusa-specific SIL document; survey wordlists of this series sometimes mark stress on each form, which would at least show whether stress position varies.

sources.citation: Galis, K. W. 1955. Talen en dialecten van Nederlands Nieuw-Guinea. Tijdschrift Nieuw-Guinea 16: 109-118, 134-145, 161-178.

sources.note: Dutch-era survey with wordlist fragments that Voorhoeve cites for the Kwerba group; unlikely but possible remark on accent.
